chapter: Sanger, Ben Black and carnival balls
title: Jimmy Dupree at the Buena Vista, Fazola, Scaglione and getting Ray Teal a job
summary: He tells of feeding Dupree, his band's late-night jam sessions, Scaglione's death, and bringing in Ray Teal to lead.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Because he was always, he'd steal an orchestration of Dave Frank and sell it to me. He came over to Biloxi when someone was playing at the Buena Vista and he puts his head in the door and he says, hey Pops. Oh I said, my God, I got this guy on my hands all summer. He came in with his clothes wrapped in the newspaper. But I wasn't eating in the hotel because I had taken a cottage because I was expecting visitors. So I told him, I said I'm entitled to three meals a day. I said please give them to this fellow. So Jimmy Dupree ate his three meals a day in the Buena Vista for free. And Fazola, the gang, took him up to an apartment they had and he slept in the bathtub. He was a bum. I said, won't you sing a song, one song for God's sake, do something for me. When the band stands, he could sing a little bit you know. I had a bunch, I had four guys in my band, played more music for nothing than they played for money. After we get through at 12 o'clock I could hear them out in the Gulf of Mexico playing on somebody's job. The drummer had a five gallon can and a couple of swatters. Fazola had his clarinet. And Skaglione had his altitude, that's a man he should have met. He died with me when I was at the jump, he died of cancer. They cut him open and closed him right away. And he was stout and he used to sweat in the coldest weather. And I used to think that he was lazy. I said you just don't want to wake. Johnny I'm suffering. He didn't suffer to me. Well one day he didn't show up. I think we got Maia Weinberg. That's when I got Maia. Maia used to kill me. He used to come to rehearsal dressed like an elephant hunter. He got a job and a puzzle on. He stuck on the girl singer I had there, bringing the flowers. He moved out to the oil station, man, 35 bucks. I said, mister I don't owe you a nickel. You go find Maia Weinberg. He said, where's that Maia Weinberg? I said, I don't know if he's doing anything about it. He's gone. I had two men in my band. I had a salary going to sheath. I had to write checks for him. I had to job. That's when I got Ray Teal a job. I had to job at the job. I was a leader. But they start changing bands, name bands. And I wanted to job. It was a nice job. So I told the manager, his name was Jimmy Lynch, that time. I said, you don't have to change band. I said, you bring a name band and it's going to cost you an awful lot of money. I said, I'll get you a name leader, Ray Teal. I said, you just build up the fact that Ray Teal has been master ceremonies at the Sanger. And we'll make something out of it. See? So I wrote Ray. And Ray was trooping around with a company. He had only five men in the orchestra. I believe he had a drum, a piano, two trumpets and a trombone. Must have been a lot. But he said it sounded good. I guess five good men in any instrumentation. If they could. But when he came down, I noticed he had a linen suit and it was all frayed in the back. He must have been on the hall. He must have been. So we wore tuxedos that looked at him. And he wore a full red suit. And he said to me, Johnny, you want to get some good tuxedo shirts cheap? I said, where? He says, at the Junior League rummage sale. He bought his shirts at the rummage sale. Can you imagine? Bought his full red suits at the rummage sale. He must have been on the hall, yeah? On the bum, huh? He must have been. And I want to tell you, prior to opening, he went around listening to other bands. I said, why are you listening to other bands? You're going to use my band. If you don't, I said, I'm going to the union, see that you don't play at all. Because Orn Tucker, you heard of Orn Tucker? Sure.
